excerpt: We then stored the texture using the OpenGL compressed format, which gives a further memory compression ratio of 1:4. The compression format lets us keep alpha values and encodes them in 4 bits. Once loaded in texture memory, each animation frame for a single human model requires 256 Kbytes. To simulate 10 different types of human with 10 frames of animation each, we need about 25 Mbytes of texture memory.
overview: These numeric constraints show the system's practical texture budget after compression. They connect frame-level storage, alpha-channel preservation, and total memory for a multi-avatar crowd, while also indicating a quality trade-off because the cited compression loses some image quality.
title: Compressed Avatar Texture Budget
